summary: US-F1: A fee schedule resolves through the hierarchy, per fee code and per channel
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** service fees defined once at the house level and bent per event,
per day and per channel, **so that** the right fees apply everywhere without editing every ticket
type.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** — (first slice of TKT-6)

This is TKT-6's third COS: *fee rules participate in the TKT-5 hierarchy*. Definition and
resolution only. The sale path is TKT-215's, payees and splits are TKT-216's, the settlement ledger
is TKT-217's.

**The model decision is this ticket's**, taken at the plan stage and recorded as an ADR in this PR
— the same shape TKT-150/ADR-036 took for pricing. ADR-036 §2 deliberately left deltas out of
pricing *because they overlap this epic*, and it already fixed the constraint any relative action
must satisfy: basis points, checked multiplication, a documented rounding direction, no floats.

**The non-obvious difference from pricing: fees are additive, prices are not.** A price resolution
has exactly one winner. A sale can carry a service fee *and* a facility fee at the same time. The
hierarchy therefore resolves **per fee code** — one winner per code, many codes per resolution —
which is what lets ADR-036's comparator be reused verbatim instead of inventing a stacking order.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] An ADR (next free number in `docs/adr/`) records the fee model: what a fee rule may express
  (the basis kinds — per-ticket fixed, per-order fixed, percentage in basis points), the rounding
  direction **and the unit it rounds at**, incidence (`passed_on` vs `absorbed`), the channel
  selector, and **which service computes the money**. It cites ADR-036 §2 for integer safety and
  either respects ADR-002's ownership row or amends it explicitly.
- [ ] A migration adds `fee_rules` to catalog: `organizer_id`-scoped, polymorphic
  `(scope_level, scope_id)` reusing ADR-036 §1's five levels, plus `fee_code`, `basis`,
  `amount` / `rate_bps`, `currency`, `incidence`, nullable `channel_code`, `priority`,
  `force_ancestor_override`, and an effective window with the same semantics as
  `price_rules` (append-mostly; `effective_until` the only mutable field, closing only).
  `amount` bounded `>= 0 AND <= 9007199254740991` (the contract's `Money` cap, ADR-028);
  `rate_bps` bounded `0..10000`; `channel_code` `length BETWEEN 1 AND 100` when non-NULL
  (ADR-024's shape). Index `(organizer_id, scope_level, scope_id)`, plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020).
- [ ] Resolution is **per fee code**: each distinct `fee_code` resolves exactly one winner via
  ADR-036 §4's comparator (specificity → forced override → priority → stable-id tiebreak);
  fees are additive across codes and never stack within one code. The comparator is a **pure,
  table-driven function** — that is the test seam, and its truth table is the test.
- [ ] Channel selectivity: a rule with `channel_code = X` is a candidate only for a request in
  channel X; a NULL-channel rule is a candidate in every channel; at the **same scope level** a
  channel-specific rule beats the channel-agnostic one, and the loser carries a reason saying so.
- [ ] A contract-declared read answers "which fees apply to this ticket type, in this channel,
  right now, and why" — winner plus losing candidates with a closed reason enum per code, the
  evaluation instant captured server-side (never a request parameter, for the same reason
  `ResolveTicketTypePrice` refuses one), and the `never` cache tier via `shared/cachetier`.
  Declared in `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`; regen committed.
- [ ] A fee rule whose `currency` differs from the ticket type's **fails the resolution loudly**
  (500, offending rule id logged and never returned) — the same disposition as
  `ErrPriceRuleCurrencyMismatch`. A misconfigured rule on a money path is never silently skipped.
- [ ] ADR-019 evidence for the new scoped read, both halves: a **poison-row result-scope** test (a
  `fee_rules` row whose `scope_id` collides with an unrelated row of a different kind is not
  loaded) **and** an `EXPLAIN`-under-`force_generic_plan` **scan** assertion over the production
  query constant, on an `ANALYZE`d seed large enough that a sequential scan is the wrong and
  expensive choice.
- [ ] A ticket type with no fee rules resolves to an **empty** fee set. Nothing about today's
  prices or reservations changes — this ticket adds no caller.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed before the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals (each has its owner):** the sale path and order totals (TKT-215) · payees and splits
(TKT-216) · the settlement ledger (TKT-217) · fee reversal on refund/exchange (carved out, see the
epic's readiness verdict) · a channel registry (ADR-024 keeps codes opaque; TKT-17 owns the registry).

objective.note: Fee schedules become authorable and resolvable through the same hierarchy prices already use, per fee code and per channel.

scope.note: Catalog only: schema + pure comparator + one read + the model ADR. No caller, no money charged, no payees.

uncertainties.note: Open by design and settled at the plan stage, recorded in the ADR: (a) the basis kinds v1 ships; (b) rounding direction and the unit it rounds at; (c) whether the resolution endpoint returns rules only or also computes amounts (which decides whether catalog needs quantity/base price as inputs); (d) whether fee rules live in a new table or a widened price_rules. Each is constrained by the ACs; none blocks starting.

dependencies.note: None. price_rules, the scope derivation and the comparator all exist at HEAD (services/catalog/internal/store/pricing.go, pricing_postgres.go, migrations 0012/0013).

approach.note: Mirror TKT-151/152's shape: pure comparator in store/pricing.go's style, DB-touching derivation in postgres.go, handler in internal/api. Reuse the existing scope derivation rather than re-deriving it.

first_slice.note: Definition + resolution with no caller is the slice that can be wrong cheaply. Everything downstream reads this shape, so getting it wrong later is a migration over rows that priced real sales.

success.note: Every AC is a state or truth-table assertion plus the two ADR-019 tests. No timing assertions.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: The pricing-rule model this epic extends. Fixes the five scope levels and how each is DERIVED from the ticket type (§1), the specificity order ticket_type > slot > series > event > venue and which parts of it are containment vs policy, the comparator steps (§4), the (scope_level, scope_id) index predicate and WHY matching on scope_id alone is a correctness bug (§3), append-mostly semantics with effective_until as the only mutable field, and - directly for this epic - §2: 'When a relative action is added, it must be integer-safe: basis points, checked multiplication, and a documented rounding direction. Floats stay banned.' It also states that deltas were deliberately left OUT of pricing because they overlap TKT-6.

The ownership line: catalog owns rule definitions, commerce owns 'pricing/fee/promo evaluation', payments owns the settlement ledger. ADR-036 §6 already amended this row once for price RESOLUTION; any further move of the line for fees must be an explicit amendment, not an assertion that the boundary did not really change.
Money is integer minor units + ISO-4217. Every fee arithmetic path is integer-only: no float, no big.Float, no decimal-as-string round trip.

Contract-first: a new operation or field must be declared in the service's openapi.yaml, and openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts regenerated and COMMITTED before the gate (check-generate diffs against HEAD).

Responses are validated against the contract and fail closed - an undeclared field or an out-of-enum header becomes a 500 with the payload withheld. A money amount above the contract's Money cap is the classic instance (ADR-036 records it as TKT-154's residue).

A scoped catalog read is only scoped if an index backs the filter, and proving it takes TWO tests: the result is scoped AND the scan is (EXPLAIN under force_generic_plan, over the production query constant, on an ANALYZEd seed big enough that a seq scan is the wrong choice).
Plain `CREATE INDEX` only - CONCURRENTLY is still not adopted, and ADR-022 satisfying precondition (1) did not change that because the preconditions are conjunctive.
Migrations run out-of-band as each binary's `migrate` subcommand, a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates.

Channel codes are EXACT OPAQUE STRINGS (1..100 chars) on inventory claims; NULL means the default/public channel. There is no channel registry and per-channel pricing/fee rules were explicitly deferred to TKT-17/TKT-5 - i.e. to this epic. Do not invent a registry here; match the existing opaque-code shape.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and the three epic-level COS
The pricing precedent to mirror: pure comparator + scope derivation + resolution handler
The price_rules schema and its effective-window migration - the shape a fee_rules table should rhyme with
Generalized EXPLAIN helper required by ADR-019 (multi-parameter, extended in place, never forked)
The cache tier registry - the `never` tier and its Cache-Control string
Channel codes as they exist today: opaque strings on inventory claims, NULL = public

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-214 (US-F1)

**Selection.** First claimable child of TKT-6 and the only one with zero open blockers: TKT-215 and
TKT-216 are both `blocked-by` this ticket, TKT-217 by those two. It also has the most unblocking
power (2 direct, 3 transitive), so the tie-break never came up.

**Blockers verified:** none open. `links: []`.

**Branch:** `TKT-214-fee-schedule-hierarchy`, cut from `origin/main` at `1d8c16c5`.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Stating it explicitly even though it is obvious, because
silence is what lets a mislabeled ticket through. This ticket adds a **money-path data model**: rows
that will decide what buyers are charged once TKT-215 consumes them, plus a **data migration** in
catalog. Two of `risk:low`'s named carve-outs (money path, data migration) apply, and the file count
will exceed five. The plan gate would be mandatory here under normal operation.

**Gates waived — this run is GATELESS, by the repo owner's instruction.** The owner has waived all
four human gates for TKT-6 and its children as a deliberate process experiment, and asked for the
waiver to be recorded in board history. Concretely:

- **Gate 1 (priority)** — given by the owner's instruction; this ticket was moved `Backlog → Ready`
  on that authority, not by a human drag.
- **Gate 2 (plan approval)** — replaced by agent judgement after the cross-model plan critique:
  prefer the option the critique recommends; where it makes no recommendation, take the most
  reversible option. Every self-made decision and its rationale is recorded in `kind=plan-final`.
- **Gate 3 (review + merge)** — the agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges,
  under the unchanged triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules. The review-guide is still posted
  first; it is the audit record.
- **Gate 4 (PO acceptance)** — self-validation of each COS against test evidence on the **merged**
  code, then the full `kind=metrics` closeout including the `overrides:` list.

Everything else in the pipeline applies unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitution,
cross-model review on both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green
before every push and after the merge, every marker comment posted, and no AI attribution in any
commit or PR.

**Model routing for this ticket**, read from `.claude/sdlc.config.json` at claim time:

| Stage | Model |
|---|---|
| `plan` | `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex) |
| `planReview` | `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5) |
| `implement` | `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5) |
| `aiReview` | `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex) |

Cross-model invariant holds on both pairs: `plan` != `planReview`, `implement` != `aiReview`. The
config was changed from `gpt-5.6-sol` to `gpt-5.6-luna` by the owner during this run (weekly plan
budget); the declared model was **probed for reachability before use** — a deliberately bogus model
name 400s on the same path, so the `--model` flag is honoured server-side and no silent substitution
is possible.

**Context-mémo revalidated at claim.** `capturedAt: 2026-08-05`, same day. `governingAdrs`
re-resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD: highest ADR is ADR-045, no fee-related ADR exists, and none
of the nine listed decisions has been superseded since the bake. The new ADR this ticket owes is
therefore **ADR-046**.

**Environment note.** The first baseline `make check` failed with `EXIT=2` — Docker daemon down, so
the smoke suite could not start. Worth recording because the harness reported that same run as
*exit 0*: the divergence AGENTS.md warns about (TKT-101) reproduced on the first gate run of this
epic. Judged from the log body, fixed by starting Docker, re-run for a real baseline.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-214 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, read-only, effort=high)**, per `config.models.plan`. Read-only
confirmed: the worktree was untouched. Condensed below; every file/symbol it cites was
independently verified at HEAD during plan-review.

#### 1. Design decision

**Recommend a separate `fee_rules` table plus a catalog-owned rule-resolution read.**

*Basis kinds:* `per_ticket_fixed` (`amount`, minor units), `per_order_fixed` (`amount`, once per
order), `percentage_bps` (`rate_bps`, `0..10000`). `amount` and `rate_bps` are mutually exclusive by
basis. `currency` always required and must match the ticket type at resolution, including on
percentage rules.

*Rounding:* **floor, at the individual ticket unit.** Worked example — two tickets at 150¢, one at
100¢, 333 bps:

| Rounding unit | Result |
|---|---|
| per ticket | 4 + 4 + 3 = **11¢** |
| per line | floor(300×333/10000) + floor(100×333/10000) = 9 + 3 = 12¢ |
| per order | floor(400×333/10000) = 13¢ |

Per-ticket rounding is the only one whose answer does not depend on how an order happens to be
grouped into lines. Checked multiplication before the divide; floats stay banned (ADR-001).

*Incidence:* `passed_on` | `absorbed`, carried on the winning rule and part of provenance. It does
**not** affect eligibility, precedence, currency validation, rounding, payee assignment or
settlement — those are TKT-215–217's.

*Channel:* exact opaque string; `NULL` is channel-agnostic and eligible in every channel; an omitted
request channel means the default/public context, where only `NULL` rules apply. Two parts —
eligibility filters out non-matching channel-specific rules, and at the *same scope level* an exact
channel match beats a channel-agnostic one. A broader exact-channel rule must **not** beat a
narrower channel-agnostic one; the distinction only applies at equal scope level. New loser reason:
`less_channel_specific`.

*Ownership:* catalog answers *"which fee rules apply, in this channel, at this instant, and why"*;
commerce computes *"what fee amount belongs in this order total"*. **ADR-002 is preserved, not
amended** — ADR-036's amendment moved only rule-based unit-price resolution.

*Separate table vs widening `price_rules`:* widening would mix one-winner absolute prices with
additive multi-code fees, fixed and percentage bases, incidence, channel selection and nullable
`amount`/`rate_bps` in one comparator, and would force migrations on a table that prices real
sales. A separate table reuses the scope derivation, window rules, index shape and precedence
machinery while keeping the two semantics distinct.

#### 2–3. DoD and files

Migration `0016_fee_rules.sql` (constraints: amount `0..9007199254740991`, rate `0..10000`, channel
length `1..100` when non-NULL, valid basis/incidence, basis-dependent nullability, valid window;
plain `CREATE INDEX fee_rules_scope ON fee_rules (organizer_id, scope_level, scope_id)`;
fail-closed Down). New `store/fees.go` (types, closed reason enum, pure per-code selection),
`store/fees_postgres.go` (write gate + `ResolveTicketTypeFees`, reusing `pricingScopesQuery`, no
time predicate in SQL), `store/store.go` port additions, `api/fees.go` handler, the OpenAPI
document + regenerated `openapi_gen.go` and both `api-types.gen.ts`, and the classification entry in
`store/public_read_invalidation_test.go`'s anti-rot map. Tests: `store/fees_test.go` (truth table),
`store/fees_smoke_test.go` (PostgreSQL), `api/fees_test.go`, `api/server_test.go` (`fakeStore`).

#### 4. Test seam and plan

Seam: **the pure per-code selector in `store/fees.go`**, mirroring `SelectPricingRule`
(`services/catalog/internal/store/pricing.go:196`) — truth-table driven, no database, no clock.

Truth table rows: no rules · one rule at each of the five levels · narrower beats broader · forced
partition · priority · stable UUID tie-break · same-level exact channel beats NULL · same-level
channel-specific with *lower* priority still wins · channel mismatch not eligible · half-open
windows at both ends · expired wrong-currency rule inert · current/future wrong-currency rule
errors. Plus per-code grouping (two rules one code → one winner + losers; two codes → two
resolutions) and input-order independence under shuffle.

> **Fixture floor, stated by the drafter:** at least two rules sharing a `fee_code` with different
> precedence, plus at least two distinct codes. A single rule per code cannot distinguish additive
> multi-code resolution from accidental single-rule behaviour.

PostgreSQL: migration constraints · scope-kind write gate · empty set (`fees: []`, not null) ·
per-code resolution · channel selectivity · currency mismatch (and the closed-window exception) ·
window flip with no write, using DB-clock-relative fixtures like
`pricing_smoke_test.go:364`.

**ADR-019 pair, both mandatory:** (1) `…DoesNotLoadScopeIDCollision` — an event whose UUID equals
the requested ticket type's, carrying an otherwise **valid, current, same-currency, plausible**
event-scoped fee rule, asserted never to appear (mirrors `pricing_smoke_test.go:207`); (2)
`…IsIndexScoped` — ≥10,000 irrelevant same-organizer rows, `ANALYZE`, the shared
`explainGenericPlan` (`season_smoke_test.go:204`, **not** forked), the **exact production query
constant**, asserting `fee_rules_scope` is used, that `Index Cond` carries both `scope_level` and
`scope_id`, and that no post-index `Filter` on `scope_id` remains. Channel filtering stays in the
pure resolver *after* the indexed five-scope read, preserving the six-parameter helper seam.

#### 5. Risks named by the draft

UUID collision / untyped predicate · percentage overflow (checked multiplication is ADR-046's
requirement; the arithmetic itself is TKT-215's) · fixture-cannot-fail (competing same-code rules
with distinguishable values; ANALYZE'd seed large enough that a seq scan is the wrong choice) ·
per-code stacking regression · NULL-channel misread as public-only · currency mismatch swallowed by
channel or window filtering · generated-contract drift · existing ticket types with no fee rules ·
polymorphic scope integrity (honest-writer, not tamper-evidence) · cache staleness.

#### 6. Open decisions the draft could not settle

1. **Fee-code vocabulary** — recommends opaque, case-sensitive, bounded, no registry/normalization
   in this ticket.
2. **Unmatched channel-specific rules in provenance** — recommends *not* returning them; adding a
   diagnostic later is additive, retracting exposed rows is not.
3. **Authoring API** — recommends store-level creation only, deferring an OpenAPI write endpoint.
4. **The public channel code** — recommends omitted channel = default/public = NULL rules only; do
   not invent a canonical `"public"` string.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Adversarial plan critique — TKT-214

**By `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.planReview`. The critic did not write the
draft and was not given the drafter's justification beyond the draft itself.

#### Seam verification (`git grep -n` at HEAD) — no hallucinated seams

| Cited | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `store/pricing.go:196` `SelectPricingRule` | ✅ exists |
| `store/pricing_postgres.go:46` `pricingScopesQuery`, `:77` candidates query | ✅ both exist |
| `store/store.go:581` price methods on the port | ✅ exists |
| `season_smoke_test.go:204` `explainGenericPlan` | ✅ exists (ADR-036 §3 cites `:201` — stale, the draft is right) |
| `pricing_smoke_test.go:146 / :207 / :364` | ✅ all three exist, and are the fallback / collision / clock-relative tests claimed |
| `api/server_test.go:698` `fakeStore.ResolveTicketTypePrice` | ✅ exists |
| `shared/go/cachetier` `Never` | ✅ exists — at `:37`, not `:31` (that is the comment). Cosmetic |
| `store/public_read_invalidation_test.go` anti-rot map | ✅ exists, and `CreatePriceRule` is already classified there with a written reason — a genuinely good catch |
| next migration `0016`, next ADR `046` | ✅ both free |

**Self-refutation check (read the draft's own Cons against its Decision): clean.** No Con in the
draft negates its own recommendation. The separate-table argument is the one place a Con could have
bitten — "row proliferation" — and it does not apply, because fee codes are additive by design.

#### Accepted without change

Separate `fee_rules` table · per-fee-code resolution (one winner per code, additive across codes) ·
the three basis kinds and their mutual exclusion · **catalog resolves rules, commerce computes
money, ADR-002 unamended** · store-level write only, no authoring endpoint · channel semantics
(exact string, NULL eligible everywhere, omitted = default/public) · ADR-036 window semantics and
the currency-check-before-window ordering with the closed-window exception · the ADR-019 pair and
its fixture floor · empty fee set as `[]`.

The rounding analysis is the strongest part of the draft and is accepted as-is: per-ticket floor is
the only unit whose answer does not depend on line grouping, and the worked cent example proves it
rather than asserting it.

#### Amendments — 7, all introduced here

**A1 [blocking] — the read must be `/internal/`, not a public route.**
The draft mirrors `price-resolution`, which is a **public, non-`/internal/`** catalog operation. But
the fee response carries `incidence: absorbed` amounts, and an absorbed fee is *the organizer's cost
structure*, not the buyer's price — what the platform and venue take out of the face value.
**TKT-155 is an open ticket recording that public price provenance is already a commercial
disclosure defect**; mirroring it here repeats that defect on strictly more sensitive data. The
draft never considered exposure, so it made no recommendation to defer to.

*Decision:* declare `GET /internal/ticket-types/{ticketTypeId}/fee-resolution` in catalog's
`openapi.yaml` with `security: []`, guarded by catalog's existing inline `X-Internal-Token` check.

*Why this is legal under ADR-043 rather than in tension with it.* ADR-043's rule is "declared
`security:` guards operations in a service's public contract; an inline check guards its internal
surface" — it constrains **where the guard lives**, not whether an internal route may be
*documented*. Commerce is the in-repo precedent for exactly this combination: 8 `/internal/` paths
**documented in its contract**, declaring no security, guarded by an inline check (ADR-043's own
table). That gives contract-first (ADR-009), response validation (ADR-028) and generated types,
while the gateway registers `/api/<svc>/internal/` to a deny handler
(`gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go:150`) so the route is fail-closed from the edge by construction.

*Credential blast radius — checked, per the mémo's TKT-190 lesson.* This adds **no new credential**.
Commerce already holds catalog's internal token and already calls
`/internal/ticket-types/{id}` with it (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:1158`,
`internal=true`). Nothing new is unlocked.

*Refusal code: **401**, not commerce's 404.* ADR-043 argues 404 is the better answer and then
explicitly declines to churn catalog's existing 401 internal routes. A new catalog route answering
404 would leave catalog with both codes — worse than either. Consistency inside one service wins;
the cross-service split stays documented and deliberate. Filed as a candidate ADR-043 amendment, not
resolved here.

*Cost, stated plainly:* absorbed-fee amounts become invisible to the storefront, so a future story
that displays *passed-on* fees to buyers will need a public projection. That is additive. Going the
other way — retracting a published public field — is a contract break. **This is the more reversible
option, and it is also the safer one**, which is why it wins on both of the tie-break rules in play.

**A2 [blocking] — do not refactor `pricing.go`'s comparator into shared helpers.**
The draft proposes extracting common precedence/ranking logic "while preserving `SelectPricingRule`
and its truth table". Rejected. (i) It edits a **shipped money path** for a ticket that adds no price
behaviour — pure regression surface against zero COS benefit. (ii) The two comparators are not the
same function: the fee one adds a channel step, groups by code, and returns a *set* rather than one
winner; a shared helper parameterized over all of that is two functions wearing one name. (iii)
AGENTS.md's rule applies squarely — *"a bounded or optimized replacement is a new implementation, so
ask what the version it replaced would have caught."* Duplicate the ~30 comparator lines in
`fees.go`, and record in ADR-046 that the duplication is deliberate, with the trigger for revisiting
it: **a third rule kind**, not a second.

**A3 [blocking] — the draft's comparator step order is wrong.**
It lists *"compare scope level first; within the same level exact channel beats NULL; then apply
ADR-036's forced partition; then priority; then id"*. The forced partition is **a filter over the
eligible set, applied before any ranking** — `pricing.go` builds `competition` before `beats` is
ever called — not a tie-break after scope comparison. Implemented as written, a forced rule would
lose to a narrower unforced one, which is the exact inversion `force_ancestor_override` exists to
prevent. Correct order:

    0. scope-pair match      4. forced partition (filter)
    1. currency (non-past)   5. scope level  (inverted if forced)
    2. window filter         6. channel specificity
    3. channel eligibility   7. priority     8. stable id

**A4 [blocking] — channel specificity under the forced partition is undefined, and that is a money
decision made by accident.**
Neither the draft nor ADR-036 says what happens when a forced channel-agnostic rule and a forced
channel-specific rule compete at the same scope level. Left undefined, `beats()` falls through to
priority and decides it silently. *Decision: channel specificity **inverts** under the forced
partition, exactly as scope rank does.* A forced rule is a house floor that refuses to be undercut,
so the **broadest** such statement is the one that binds — and a channel-agnostic rule is the
broader statement. The truth table owes this row.

**A5 [blocking] — the plan misses catalog's coverage gate (ADR-030).**
`services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go` fails the whole suite for any documented 2xx
operation with no happy-path test driving it through `env.do`. A newly declared operation therefore
**cannot** ship without an API test, and `fakeStore` must implement the new `Store` methods or the
package will not compile. The draft names `fakeStore` but not the gate that makes it mandatory —
this is the most likely way the first `make check` run fails.

**A6 [minor] — one spelling for the query parameter.** The draft writes `?channel_code=` in the
contract line and `channel` in a handler test. Use `channel_code` throughout, matching the column
and ADR-024's vocabulary.

**A7 [minor] — zero-amount fees are still fees.** `floor(amount × bps / 10000)` is `0` for small
amounts (1¢ at 333 bps). ADR-046 must state that a resolved fee of amount 0 is still a resolved fee
and still appears in the breakdown with its code and payee. Otherwise a fee code blinks out of
existence as a function of price, and TKT-216/217 inherit a payee that is sometimes owed nothing and
sometimes absent — two different states that would look identical.

#### Rejected

None. Every part of the draft is either accepted or amended; nothing in it is a false statement
about the code.

#### Pre-mortem lens (per `quality-practices.md` §1)

*Assume the PR bounced. Why?* Five plausible causes, each now patched above:

1. First `make check` fails on the **coverage gate** — a declared operation with no driving test →
   A5.
2. `make check` fails on **codegen drift** — regeneration not committed before the gate. Sequence is
   fixed in the DoD: implement → `make generate` → **commit** → gate.
